papers.title: From business intelligence to conservation intelligence: Operationalizing adaptive pest control of crown‐of‐thorns starfish to protect the resilience of the Great Barrier Reef
papers.authors: Samuel A. Matthews, Roger Beeden, Mary C. Bonin, Camille Mellin, Morgan Stuart Pratchett
papers.abstract: Abstract Resilience‐based management (RBM)—which focuses explicitly on preserving and actively enhancing an ecosystem's capacity to resist and recover from cumulative disturbances under climate change—is crucial for enhancing outcomes in conservation interventions as the climate changes. To be effective it requires continuous modeling, assessment, evaluation and adjustment. Here, we deploy enterprise Business Intelligence software for the purpose of conservation (i.e., Conservation Intelligence) to provide the near real‐time analytics and decision support system necessary for effective RBM. This approach is demonstrated using the Crown‐of‐Thorns Starfish Control Program on Australia's Great Barrier Reef where integrated visual dashboards were developed to assess outbreak severity, prioritize control actions, evaluate effectiveness and incorporate emerging research to close the research‐implementation gap. The flexibility of Business Intelligence software allows these Conservation Intelligence tools to be built and maintained “in‐house,” meeting the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority's (GBRMPA) explicit needs and reducing dependency on external developers or researchers. papers.title: Dynamic Natural-Capital Accounting under Tipping Risk and Spatial Contagion: A Regenerative Forest Network Model
papers.authors: Jules Sadefo Kamdem
papers.abstract: Abstract Classical renewable-resource models value the biological stock that remains after current extraction, whereas ecological resilience theory emphasizes the possibility of alternative regimes separated by tipping boundaries. This paper combines these perspectives in a networked forest-management problem with two continuous ecological states---harvestable biomass and resilience---and a discrete ecological regime for each patch. Harvesting lowers biomass and resilience and increases the endogenous intensity of a harmful regime shift; regenerative effort rebuilds ecological capital and reduces that intensity. The hazard also rises with exposure to degraded neighboring patches, generating spatial contagion. The planner solves an infinite-horizon controlled piecewise-deterministic Markov decision problem. Rather than assuming positive ecological shadow values, we derive them from primitive order conditions by monotone dynamic programming. Six structural results follow. papers.title: Functional and numerical responses of Cydnoseius negevi (Swirski and Amitai) to three invasive pests
papers.authors: Marwa El-Desouky Barghout, Huda Hassan Elbehery, İsmail Döker, Mahmoud Ramadan, Islam Zidan
papers.abstract: Agricultural system in Egypt represents a promising alternative for addressing water scarcity and land limitations. However, these systems are increasingly affected by invasive pest species including the two-spotted spider mite (TSSM), Tetranychus urticae Koch (Prostigmata: Tetranychidae), the onion thrips, Thrips tabaci Lindeman (Thysanoptera: Thripidae), and the silverleaf whitefly, Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae). This study evaluated the functional and numerical responses of the native predatory mite, Cydnoseius negevi (Swirski and Amitai) (Mesostigmata: Phytoseiidae) to different densities of these three invasive pest species under laboratory conditions. Predation assays were conducted using prey densities 1, 5, 10, 20, 40, and 80 individuals. Functional response parameters including attack rate (α) and handling time (Th), were estimated using nonlinear regression, and numerical responses were analysed using generalized linear models using R program. Cydnoseius negevi exhibited a Type II functional response to all prey species. papers.title: Detection of field parasitism of the invasive spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula) by native North American wasps using molecular tools
papers.authors: Yunke Wu, Hannah J. Broadley, Caroline E. Davock, Megan E. Doner, Brian E. Silva
papers.abstract: Abstract The management of invasive pest species frequently involves biological control to suppress the expanding pest populations. Although introduced natural enemies have been favored, the role of native fauna should not be overlooked. The spotted lanternfly ( Lycorma delicatula White; Hemiptera: Fulgoridae) is an invasive, polyphagous plant pest that has rapidly spread across eastern USA over the past decade. Biological control efforts of this pest largely focus on imported parasitoids, but there is increasing evidence of native wasps attacking spotted lanternfly eggs in the USA. To obtain a more accurate estimate of parasitism by one native wasp, Anastatus reduvii (Howard) (Hymenoptera: Eupelmidae), we developed a duplex real-time PCR (qPCR) assay capable of detecting A. reduvii DNA in spotted lanternfly eggs. In silico analysis and non-target testing using three additional Anastatus spp. and five potential host species indicated a low likelihood of false positive amplification. We applied the qPCR assay to spotted lanternfly eggs with parasitoid emergence holes collected from 11 locations in southeastern Pennsylvania, USA that encompass over 6000 km 2 . papers.authors: Beatriz E. Nobua-Behrmann, John N. Kabashima
papers.abstract: Abstract Invasive shothole borers ( Euwallacea spp.)(ISHB) and their associated fungal pathogens cause substantial damage to urban and riparian trees, creating a need for diverse management approaches to accommodate different infestation scenarios. Gallery injection, a technique in which small volumes of pesticide are delivered directly into active beetle galleries, has not previously been evaluated for ISHB and may provide a localized treatment option that limits pesticide applications to infested portions of the host. The objective of this study was to evaluate gallery injection as a management approach for ISHB, compare the efficacy of different active ingredients delivered using this method, and quantify the volume of solution that could be delivered into active galleries under field conditions. Field trials were conducted on Platanus spp. in Southern California. Active galleries were verified prior to treatment, and beetle activity was assessed following injections. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.authors: Annie E. Prescott
papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can be mitigated. One way to reduce wildfire risks and protect life, property, and ecosystem services is through fuel treatments — actions that reduce the amount and arrangement of flammable vegetation through mechanical removal, wildland fire, or other methods. Information on wildfire behavior and fuel treatments is abundant but often scattered, ecosystem-specific and difficult to access. In addition, most research in the Western U.S. has focused on conifer forests, leaving other vegetation types understudied. This research addresses these gaps by summarizing wildfire and fuel treatment information for Utah and examining how fuels treatments and wildfire affect wildlands dominated by Gambel oak and bigtooth maple. Chapter II presents a practical guide to wildfire and fuel management in Utah. papers.title: ADVANCING BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION IN A RAPIDLY CHANGING WORLD: PLANT-CENTERED STRATEGIES FOR ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE, RESTORATION AND SUSTAINABLE FUTURE
papers.authors: Shubham Kumar, Astuti Tiwari, Shubhangi Tripathi, Apoorva Choudhary, Sanjeev Kumar
papers.source: OpenAlex / SARPS Journal of Advanced Research in Plant Science
papers.abstract: Biodiversity conservation is shifting from the paradigm of species protection to the maintenance of ecological, genetic, and functional integrity. Earlier biodiversity research and conservation practice focused on understanding and responding to the drivers of biodiversity loss, e.g., habitat loss, climate change, environmental degradation, invasive species, and overexploitation. This review synthesizes the role of plants in sustaining ecosystems, with an emphasis on genetic conservation, ecological restoration, connectivity, conservation biotechnology, monitoring, and adaptive governance. The current crisis of biodiversity loss affects a million species, threatening their extinction, while plant genetic diversity is also disappearing at an alarming rate. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) Third Report on the State of the World’s Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, 42% of the plant genetic resources evaluated for taxonomic diversity were no longer present in at least one country. papers.title: A privacy aware lightweight edge intelligent framework for real-time lethal threat interception and risk assessment
papers.authors: Himadri Nath Saha, Utsho Banerjee, Ayush Ghosh, Ebrahim Abdulla Mattar, Pronoya Bhattacharya
papers.abstract: Real-time intelligent surveillance systems require a careful balance between predictive reliability, computational efficiency, energy consumption, inference latency, and privacy preservation. However, existing vision-based approaches often achieve high detection accuracy at the expense of computational complexity, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this challenge, we propose a privacy-preserving, lightweight edge intelligence framework guided by a multi-objective architectural design methodology that jointly balances accuracy, computational efficiency, energy efficiency, real-time responsiveness, and on-device privacy.​ The proposed framework combines hybrid local-global representation learning with a lightweight multi-scale spatial attention mechanism to enhance the recognition of small and partially occluded lethal threats. A lightweight Temporal Threat Validation Module suppresses transient false alarms through temporal consistency analysis, while a context-aware Threat Assessment Network transforms validated detections into quantitative threat intelligence for priority-based decision-making. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.title: Mycotoxin contamination in cereals and oil crops: mycotoxigenic fungi, geographic distribution, and green control strategies
papers.authors: Meng-Meng Yang, Ming-Jun Zhao, Zhuo Du, Xue Meng-yao, Zheng Qu
papers.source: OpenAlex / Mycology&#58 An International Journal on Fungal Biology
papers.abstract: Cereals and oil crops play a critical role in the global food system, providing essential energy and nutrition for a vast population. However, during growth and storage, these crops are susceptible to infection by toxigenic fungi, which subsequently produce mycotoxins, posing serious threats to human and animal health. This review systematically summarizes the common toxigenic fungi and their associated mycotoxins in cereals and oil crops, covering their geographical distribution, toxic effects, and contamination status. Furthermore, the article discusses integrated prevention and control strategies for mycotoxin contamination spanning pre- and post-harvest stages, with a focus on key measures such as breeding, crop rotation, biological control, and novel storage technologies, emphasizing the importance of developing green control techniques. Finally, this review highlights the strategic significance of establishing robust monitoring systems, formulating science-based regulatory policies, and strengthening international cooperation to mitigate the risks of mycotoxin contamination.

papers.title: Changes in species composition 20 years after selection cutting in northern hardwood and mixedwood stands
papers.authors: Simon Bilodeau‐Gauthier, François Guillemette, Steve Bédard
papers.abstract: Temperate forests of northeastern North America provide key ecosystem services but are increasingly affected by multiple stressors, including climate change, biological invasions, pollution, and land-use impacts, potentially altering species composition and thus productivity and sustainability of these forests. This study examined 20-year compositional changes in 233 uneven-aged forest stands subjected to single-tree selection (STS) cutting or left unmanaged, encompassing hardwood and mixedwood stands across southern Quebec, Canada. Analyses were based on species-specific proportions of basal area across three developmental stages: saplings, recruit trees, and pre-existing canopy trees. Results indicated that compositional shifts primarily occurred in younger cohorts (saplings and recruits), while canopy composition remained relatively stable. In hardwood stands, the proportion of sugar maple ( Acer saccharum Marsh.) declined among recruits and saplings, whereas that of American beech ( Fagus grandifolia Ehrh.) increased, indicating a gradual replacement dynamic. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. papers.authors: Rong-Kun Zhu, Wen-hao Yin, Hongjian Zhou, Ling Ge, Hui Zeng
papers.source: OpenAlex / Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
papers.abstract: Intracranial aneurysm are acquired dilatations of cerebral arteries that may rupture and cause subarachnoid hemorrhage. Their progression involves hemodynamic stress, endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, smooth muscle cell loss, extracellular matrix degradation, and maladaptive repair. Although inflammatory activation has been widely studied, the failure of inflammation resolution remains poorly understood. Efferocytosis, the clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages and neighboring cells, is essential for resolving inflammation and maintaining tissue homeostasis. When efferocytosis is impaired, apoptotic cells undergo secondary necrosis, releasing damage-associated signals that sustain inflammation. In intracranial aneurysms, oxidative stress, hypoxia, protease activation, intraluminal thrombus, inflammatory cytokines, macrophage dysfunction, HMGB1, MerTK cleavage, and reduced bridging molecules such as Gas6, Protein S, and MFG-E8 may compromise efferocytosis. papers.title: A TaqMan assay that knows its mite: specific detection of Tropilaelaps mercedesae Clade I
papers.authors: Marga P. E. van Gent‐Pelzer, Marc Hendriks, Terd Disayathanoowat, Patcharin Phokasem, Heather Graham
papers.abstract: Abstract Tropilaelaps mercedesae ( Mesostigmata : Laelapidae ), an invasive mite native to Southeast Asia, is spreading rapidly due to global bee trade and climate change. Its detection in Eastern Europe raises concerns about its entry into the EU. As a notifiable parasite under EU Animal Health Law, early and reliable detection is essential. We developed a sensitive TaqMan assay targeting the cytochrome C oxidase subunit I (COI) gene, using synthetic double-stranded DNA fragments (gBlocks). This assay enables rapid, specific, and scalable detection of T. mercedesae Clade I.

papers.abstract: Impaired pulmonary epithelial cell homeostasis is a key pathogenic feature in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Mucin 1 (MUC1/Muc1) is a membrane-tethered glycoprotein that plays important roles in modulating various disease progression. This study aims to decipher the role and mechanisms of MUC1 in the pathogenesis of COPD. We found functional variants (rs4072037 T > C and rs12411216 C > A) in MUC1 were associated with increased susceptibility to COPD. MUC1-C expression in lung tissues was age-dependent, elevated in adults but decreased in elderly COPD patients. Aged Muc1-deficient mice showed increased cellular senescence in alveolar type II (AT2) epithelial cells and spontaneously developed emphysema. In cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD model mice, Muc1 deficiency caused an accelerated decline in lung function, impaired mitochondrial function, enhanced lung inflammation, and impaired AT2-to- alveolar type I (AT1) epithelial cell transdifferentiation. papers.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screening in Spodoptera frugiperda reveals the determinants of insecticide activation and sensitivity
papers.authors: Huidong Wang, Yueru Ye, Tong Zhang, Bingbing Li, Angela Hayward
papers.abstract: Insecticide resistance poses a growing threat to global human health and food security. Addressing this challenge requires a comprehensive understanding of the molecular determinants that govern insecticide action and insect sensitivity. However, identifying and functionally validating the specific genes - among the tens of thousands present in a typical insect genome - that contribute to insecticide mode of action and resistance remains a major challenge. Here, we present a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening system in a cell line derived from Spodoptera frugiperda, a highly damaging insect pest, and demonstrate its utility for dissecting the molecular basis of insecticide activity and resistance. We construct a library of 90,759 single guide RNAs (sgRNAs) targeting 14,434 genes and conduct a three-round screen under successively increasing concentrations of the insecticide pyridalyl. This enriches for the cytochrome P450 gene CYP333B4. Subsequent P450 inhibitor assays, gene knockout in S. frugiperda, and ectopic expression in Drosophila melanogaster confirm that members of the CYP333B subfamily are key mediators of pyridalyl activation and serve as potential resistance targets.

papers.authors: Adil Zia, Muhammad Usman, Safdar Ali, Muhammad Kamran, Sajid Aleem Khan
papers.abstract: Abstract Wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) is the principal staple crop of Pakistan, with Punjab contributing approximately 75% of the country's total wheat production. Leaf rust ( Puccinia triticina ) and stripe rust ( Puccinia striiformis ) are among the most detrimental diseases affecting wheat yield in the country. papers.abstract: Rainfall variability has implications for agricultural planning and water resource management in Nasarawa State, Nigeria. This study examined rainfall trends, interannual variability, and growing-season dynamics over the 27-year period from 1997 to 2023. Monthly rainfall and rainy-day data obtained from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency were used to assess annual rainfall totals, rainy-day counts, rainfall onset and cessation, and length of growing season (LGS). Variability was examined across two subperiods, 1997–2010 and 2011–2023, while trends and statistical significance were assessed using linear regression and Student’s t-test. papers.authors: Joanna Miller Smallwood, Evan Killick, Alexander Antonarakis, Ana Mariscal, Fiona Mathews
papers.abstract: Abstract Rights of Nature (RoN) is increasingly used to challenge conventional legal frameworks, restructure governance over ecosystems and living beings, and rethink human–nature relations; however, its role in addressing human–wildlife conflict remains undertheorized and insufficiently defined. Using the case of the Andean (spectacled) bear ( Tremarctos ornatus ) in Ecuador’s Andean Bear Corridor, and the emerging conflict between individual bears and local farmers, this article presents an innovative RoN framework for conflict governance. The research employs a socio-legal approach – doctrinal analysis, qualitative interdisciplinary fieldwork (2022–2025) across five local communities in the Ecuadorian Andes and informal expert interviews – to compile a set of rights at multiple scales (ecosystem, species, individual animal) and identifies relevant principles of human–wildlife conflicts based on jurisprudence. papers.authors: Johann Lallemand, Bruno B. Chauvel, Guillaume Adeux, Saskia Bastin, Guillaume Fried
papers.abstract: L’article relate la première observation d’Amaranthus tuberculatus en métropole, sur une parcelle expérimentale INRAE. L’espèce est comparée aux autres amarantes historiquement observées en France et en Europe. Des informations sur l’historique de sa propagation, ses préférences écologiques et ses caractéristiques biologiques sont fournies. De par sa forte capacité de production de graines, son caractère dioïque, sa faculté de résistance aux herbicides et son fort potentiel compétitif sur les cultures, une attention accrue est nécessaire pour éviter son installation sur le territoire français.

papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming modern society including animal genetics and breeding which is essential for meeting global nutritional needs in supplying milk, meat, and eggs among the most complete sources of protein and micronutrients. Although animal breeding has a long history of using data-driven prediction methods, the application of modern AI approaches remains at a relatively early stage and shows substantial potential for wide-ranging applications in animal genetics and breeding. This study aims to review the current use of AI tools in livestock species across three major applications of high interest: AI-assisted phenotyping, AI-enabled dissection of complex-trait biology (focusing on AI-assisted GWAS and AI-for-omics), and AI-assisted genomic prediction. In addition, we discussed emerging methods and tools developed in human genetics that are not yet widely adopted in farm animals but may offer translational potential for future livestock studies. papers.authors: Reena Dubey, Anne Zaar, Riccardo Zustovi, Kevin Dewitte, Jasper Vlerick
papers.abstract: Abstract Faba bean ( Vicia faba L.) is a high-protein legume suited to Northwestern Europe, yet adoption is hindered by limited winter survival, acute cold events, and seed anti-nutritional factors notably vicine and convicine (VC) that constrain food use despite high protein content. We conducted a two-year, two-season study in Belgium (2022–2024) directly comparing winter versus spring accessions via field phenotyping, intact-seed NIRS (n=343), and standardized breadmaking (10% wheat-flour substitution). Winter accessions experienced pronounced cold stress, exhibited slower photothermal growth, and nonetheless produced higher thousand-kernel weight, whereas spring accessions flowered more synchronously and gained height faster per unit thermal time. Culture and microscopy of symptomatic stems indicated that ≈75% of winter injuries were abiotic cold shock, not pathogen mediated. papers.abstract: Solitary-phase Oedaleus asiaticus (Bei-Bienko) can switch to the far more destructive gregarious phase as population density rises, posing a serious threat to agriculture, animal husbandry and local economies. The current investigation assessed how developmental stages and population density impacted phase transitions and which genes served as key regulatory elements of this process. The results showed that the younger nymphs were, the higher proportion that shifted from solitary to gregarious phase, whereas adults never switched; a density of 60 insects produced the highest transition rate, whereas lower or higher densities resulted in fewer gregarious individuals. The gregarious locusts maintained their original physical characteristics when they were grown in solitary conditions. papers.authors: Qudrat Ullah, Esha Arshad, Kainat Fatima, Waqas Haider, Muhammad Qasim
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of soil science and plant nutrition
papers.abstract: The depletion of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the escalating prevalence of soil-borne plant pathogens represent critical challenges to terrestrial biogeochemical stability and global food security. With approximately 24% of terrestrial carbon reserves lost and over US$220 billion in annual crop losses attributed to soil-borne diseases, understanding biotic and geochemical controls on soil health is essential. This review evaluates the dual functionality of organic amendments (agricultural residues, animal manures, and urban biosolids) as drivers of simultaneous carbon restoration and pathogen suppression. We analyze the mechanisms governing these benefits, focusing on the biogeochemical coupling of element cycles and microbiome-mediated processes such as the formation of recalcitrant carbon, organo-mineral protection, and microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE). Biochar applications can increase SOC stocks by 26–33% (11.5–14.6 Mg ha⁻¹), while silicon-modified biochar reduces the bacterial wilt index caused by Ralstonia solanacearum by 73.4%. Furthermore, we examine the geochemical mechanisms of pathogen suppression through antibiosis, resource competition, and signaling disruption.

papers.abstract: Precise biophysical characterization of non-enveloped viruses and virus-like particles (VLPs) is essential for evaluating assembly, structural integrity, and sample heterogeneity - key parameters that influence infectivity, manufacturability, and therapeutic performance. Analytical ultracentrifugation, light scattering, and mass photometry provide complementary information on particle size distributions, empty/full ratios, and assembly quality. Native and charge-detection mass spectrometry extend this, enabling accurate mass determination and genome-loading assessment. Solution-based structural techniques, such as SAXS and spectroscopy, provide dynamics. High-resolution X-ray crystallography, cryogenic electron microscopy, and tomography reveal global architectures, quaternary arrangements, and conformational switching essential for entry and maturation. Besides these methods, atomic force microscopy also allows nanoscale visualization in conjunction with mechanical profiling, linking physical stability with functional behavior. papers.title: Viral infections as gatekeepers of bacterial infections in otitis media: Immune mechanisms and implications for therapeutic interventions
papers.authors: Ayesha Zahid, Hazrat Ismail, Jennifer C. Wilson, Irwin Darren Grice
papers.abstract: Otitis media (OM) is a highly prevalent inflammatory disease of the human middle ear and a key contributor to poor health outcomes in young children on a global scale. While bacterial pathogens such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis are well-recognised contributors to OM, increasing evidence highlights respiratory viruses as critical gatekeepers that predispose the middle ear to bacterial infection. Viral upper respiratory infections initiate mucosal inflammation, disrupt epithelial barrier integrity and mucociliary clearance, and alter host immunological responses. Collectively, these changes create a permissive environment for bacterial colonization, ascension, and persistence within the middle ear. Viral and bacterial coinfections are commonly found and are linked to poorer clinical outcomes, extended inflammation, and increased disease severity. This review synthesises current evidence on the mechanisms by which viruses prime the middle ear for subsequent bacterial infections, with particular emphasis on epithelial dysfunction, receptor modulation, interferon-driven immune responses, and alterations in innate immune training. papers.title: GFR-SAM: Training-Free Referring Camouflaged Object Segmentation via Cross-Image Prompting

papers.source: OpenAlex / ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
papers.abstract: Referring Camouflaged Object Detection (Ref-COD) requires segmenting hidden targets guided by reference cues. While supervised methods are annotation-heavy and training-free approaches via sparse point-prompting are sensitive to localization errors, we propose GFR-SAM, a robust three-stage training-free framework. GFR-SAM shifts the paradigm from fragile point-matching to a "Generate-Filter-Refine" pipeline. First, we introduce In-Context Exemplar-guided Segmentation, empowering SAM3 with cross-image inference to generate candidate masks via holistic visual exemplars, bypassing its native intra-image constraints. Second, a Region-Global Contrastive Filtering module ranks candidates through DINOv3-based prototypical alignment, effectively suppressing background distractors. Finally, a Geometric-Semantic Refinement module synergizes bounding box and text prompts to recover fine-grained boundaries and enhance instance recall. Evaluated on the R2C7K benchmark, GFR-SAM outperforms existing training-free methods by 8.7% in weighted F-measure (F ? w ) and competes with supervised state-of-the-art counterparts. papers.title: From detection to decision: molecular, genomic, and AI innovations for managing Ganoderma boninense in oil palm
papers.authors: Qudrat Ullah, Waqas Haider, Farhang Hameed Awlqadr, Ahmed Bilal, Muhammad Tayyab Arshad
papers.abstract: Ganoderma boninense causes basal stem rot (BSR) in oil palm, resulting in substantial economic losses, particularly for smallholders who contribute approximately 40% of global production. This review synthesizes advances in molecular diagnostic techniques (qPCR, LAMP), whole-genome sequencing of resistant Elaeis guineensis genotypes, and AI-driven remote sensing to enhance understanding of G. boninense pathobiology. Soilborne mycelia of the pathogen can persist for more than 10 y. Asymptomatic infections, which are frequently missed by conventional methods, can lead to significant disease spread within plantations over 2 y. CRISPR-based paper-strip tests have demonstrated high sensitivity (detecting < 1 pg DNA in laboratory settings), while marker-assisted selection has helped identify additional resistance QTLs. Trichoderma biofilms and biodegradable fumigants reduced soil inoculum by 50–75% in controlled studies. AI-based decision support systems have demonstrated promising accuracy for guiding interventions and potential cost savings, although further field validation across diverse conditions is needed.

Results The results showed that bacterial community dynamics were significantly influenced by compartment and disease stage. Also in stem compartment, the late stage was characterized by marked enrichment of the phylum Proteobacteria, accompanied by elevated relative abundances of the genera Pseudomonas and Methylobacterium .
